description: A worker stops on a decision that touches code (a cache pool in a pull request) and an issue (the connection budget held in triage). The decision JSON carries what only the coordinator knows: a topic, the components around the decision as an architecture, a kind on each step of how it got here, and a kind on each reference. What the page can read for itself (when it was asked, the answer, a reference's status) is left to the page.
prompt:
<cross-session-message from="uds:/tmp/cc-socks/6021.sock" from-name="impl-cache" from-mode="prompting">
Stopped before asking for merge. PR #58 adds a warm pool of 20 database connections (src/cache/pool.py:24-58), which the cache client (src/cache/client.py) draws from; its pipeline passed and it has one approval. Review asked how many connections the database allows: the limit is 320 (config/db.toml:14). docs/architecture.md §4.2 caps each service's connections, but no cap is set yet; issue #111 tracks that budget and is held in triage. Without the pool the first request after a deploy takes 9 to 14 seconds; with it, 180 ms. Keep the pool of 20, start cold, or a pool of 5? Nothing merges until that is decided.
</cross-session-message>

graders.name: no render step: the server renders
the decision names its topic
graders.rule: The JSON holds `headline`, `topic` (the area it is in, in a word or two), ...

graders.name: the components around the decision are drawn
graders.rule: When the ask concerns components, `architecture` draws them: `nodes` (...), `edges` (...), `summary` and `not_drawn`.

graders.name: each step of how it got here has a kind
graders.rule: `timeline` (`when`, `text`, `kind`: the lane stage the step happened in, or `hot` for what went wrong): each step that led to the ask, from the Log, the messages and the forge

graders.name: each reference has a kind
graders.rule: `references` (`kind`: issue, PR, MR, code, doc, note, pipeline or commit, `value`, `label`)

graders.name: the page is never an artifact
